Вам потрібне більш детальне пояснення кожного з них?<#sep#>user: Los 5 principios clave de Six Sigma
La metodología Six Sigma tiene 5 principios clave que puedes aplicar cuando analices tus procesos.

1. Poner el foco en el cliente
En Six Sigma, el objetivo es garantizar que puedes brindar a los clientes el mayor valor posible. Es decir, tu equipo debería dedicar mucho tiempo a identificar quiénes son tus clientes, cuáles son sus necesidades y qué los motiva a comprar productos. Este principio, funciona perfectamente también para compañías de SaaS, ya que, con frecuencia, se centran en flujos de ingresos recurrentes. Al identificar lo que el cliente quiere y necesita, el equipo puede entender mejor cómo retenerlo y hacer que vuelva constantemente al producto.

Para lograrlo, el equipo debe entender cuál es la calidad del producto que tus clientes consideran aceptable, a fin de poder cumplir o, incluso, exceder sus expectativas. Una vez que conozcas ese nivel de calidad, podrás utilizarlo como punto de referencia para la producción.

2. Usar los datos para detectar dónde se produce la variación
Detalla todos los pasos del proceso de producción actual. Una vez que lo hayas hecho, analiza y reúne los datos de ese proceso para ver si hay áreas que se puedan optimizar o que estén provocando cuellos de botella en el flujo de trabajo. Por ejemplo, evalúa cómo compartes la información con el equipo. ¿Todos reciben la misma información o hay documentos de referencia que están desactualizados? Al establecer un lugar central para toda la información pertinente del proyecto, se minimiza la cantidad de tiempo dedicado a buscar los documentos correctos.

A veces, puede resultar complicado decidir cuáles son las métricas que conviene analizar. Una manera muy simple de descubrirlo es con el trabajo en retrospectiva. Identifica un objetivo que quieres alcanzar y determina los trabajos a partir de allí hacia atrás. Por ejemplo, si el objetivo es reducir el tiempo de producción, analiza cuánto tiempo toma cada paso de ese proceso.

3. Mejorar los procesos continuamente
Mientras observas tus procesos de producción, piensa en los pasos que no aportan valor al equipo o a los clientes finales. Usa herramientas como los mapas de flujo de valor para identificar cómo puedes perfeccionar los procesos y reducir la cantidad de cuellos de botella.

La idea de hacer pequeñas mejoras a los procesos a lo largo del tiempo se conoce como Kaizen o mejora continua. La filosofía detrás de la mejora continua indica que si haces pequeños cambios durante un período prolongado, a la larga se transformarán en grandes cambios positivos.

4. Incluir a todos
Six Sigma es una metodología que ofrece la misma posibilidad de contribuir a todos los integrantes de un equipo. Pero todos deben recibir capacitación en procesos Six Sigma, para disminuir los riesgos de crear más obstáculos en vez de eliminarlos.

Six Sigma funciona particularmente bien cuando se trabaja con equipos interdisciplinarios, porque brinda una visión integral de cómo un mismo proceso puede afectar a las distintas partes del negocio. Cuando incluyes representantes de todos los equipos que participan en el proceso, ofreces a cada uno los detalles de las mejoras y el impacto que esos cambios pueden tener en sus equipos.

5. Garantizar un ambiente flexible y receptivo
Six Sigma se centra en crear cambios positivos para los clientes. Significa que debes buscar continuamente formas de mejorar los procesos, y el equipo entero debe ser siempre flexible para poder dar un giro, cuando sea necesario, siempre sin demasiados inconvenientes.

También significa que los procesos deben ser fácilmente intercambiables. Una forma sencilla de lograrlo es separando los procesos en pasos. Si hay un problema con uno solo de los pasos, entonces, solamente habrá que arreglar ese paso y no el proceso completo.

Las 2 principales metodologías Six Sigma
Hay dos procesos comunes dentro de Six Sigma y cada uno se usa en una situación diferente. El método DMAIC es el estándar que se usa cuando hay que optimizar los procesos existentes. El otro método, el DMADV, se aplica cuando los procesos aún no se han establecido y todavía hay que crearlos.

La metodología se enfoca en brindar el mayor valor posible al cliente y en analizar los procesos para identificar cuellos de botella y oportunidades de mejora. Six Sigma es una metodología que permite la contribución de todos los miembros del equipo y es efectiva cuando se trabaja con equipos interdisciplinarios.<#sep#>user: Kindly analyse the ways in which the game Mancala/ Oware can aid in numeracy and strategic thinking. The phrase "a monoid in the class of endofunctors" refers to the fact that the operation of combining two monads can be thought of as a monoid operation, where the elements of the monoid are the endofunctors. Specifically, the operation of combining two monads T and S is given by the composition of their endofunctors T(S(-)).

user: What exactly is a monad in terms of functional programming in Haskell? What relation does it have with the mathematical concept of a monad?

assistant: In Haskell, a monad is a way of structuring computations, particularly in situations where a sequence of computations may have side effects or where the order of execution matters.

A monad in Haskell is defined as a type class that provides two operations: `return` and `(>>=)` (pronounced "bind"). The `return` operation takes a value and wraps it in a monadic context, while the `(>>=)` operation takes a monadic value and a function that operates on the underlying value, and returns a new monadic value. The key feature of a monad is that it allows for sequencing of computations, where the output of one computation is passed as input to the next computation.

The mathematical concept of a monad provides a theoretical underpinning for the use of monads in functional programming. In category theory, a monad is a way of composing functors in a certain way, as I mentioned in my previous answer. This composition of functors can be thought of as a way of structuring computations in a category-theoretic setting.

In functional programming, the monad structure provides a way of structuring computations in a way that is both composable and modular. By using the operations provided by the monad, we can chain together computations in a way that is easy to reason about and that allows us to encapsulate side effects.

In essence, the Haskell concept of a monad is a concrete implementation of the abstract mathematical concept of a monad, adapted to the specific needs of functional programming.

1. Maybe Monad: This is perhaps the most well-known example of a monad in Haskell. The Maybe monad is used to handle computations that might fail, by representing a computation that can either return a value or nothing at all.
2. IO Monad: The IO monad is used for input and output operations in Haskell. It allows for side-effectful computations, such as reading and writing files, interacting with the network, and more.
3. List Monad: The List monad is used to represent computations that can return multiple results. It allows for chaining of computations that generate lists, such as filtering, mapping, and folding.

These are just a few examples of the many monads available in Haskell. assistant: Dutch Trademark Law: An Introduction

Dutch trademark law plays a crucial role in safeguarding the intellectual property rights of businesses and individuals in the Netherlands. The primary piece of legislation governing trademarks in the country is the Benelux Convention on Intellectual Property (BCIP), which harmonizes trademark laws across the Benelux countries: Belgium, the Netherlands, and Luxembourg. Additionally, Dutch trademark law is influenced by European Union (EU) regulations, directives, and jurisprudence, as the Netherlands is an EU member state. This brief introduction will provide an overview of Dutch trademark law, including the trademark registration process, scope of protection, and enforcement mechanisms.

Trademark Registration

In the Netherlands, trademark protection is granted through registration with the Benelux Office for Intellectual Property (BOIP). While it is possible to acquire limited rights through the actual use of a trademark, registering a trademark provides the owner with stronger and more extensive legal protection.

The registration process begins with a trademark search to ensure the proposed mark does not conflict with existing trademarks. If the search results are favorable, the applicant can proceed with filing the application, including providing the necessary information, such as the trademark, its representation, the applicant's details, and the goods and services the trademark will cover, classified according to the Nice Classification system.

After the application is submitted, the BOIP examines it for compliance with the formal requirements and conducts a limited substantive examination, focusing on absolute grounds for refusal. Examples of absolute grounds for refusal include lack of distinctiveness, descriptiveness, genericness, or the trademark being contrary to public policy or accepted principles of morality. If the application satisfies the requirements and passes the examination, the trademark is registered, published in the Benelux Trademark Register, and protected for ten years from the filing date. Trademark protection can be renewed indefinitely, in ten-year increments, by paying the applicable renewal fees.

Scope of Trademark Protection

Registered trademarks in the Netherlands are protected against unauthorized use by third parties. The owner of a registered trademark has the exclusive right to use the trademark for the goods and services for which it is registered. Trademark protection extends to cases where a third party uses a similar or identical sign for identical or similar goods and services, and there is a likelihood of confusion among consumers, including the possibility of association with the registered trademark.

Infringement and Enforcement

Trademark owners have several legal avenues for enforcing their rights against infringers in the Netherlands. Cease and desist letters, negotiations, and alternative dispute resolution methods, such as mediation and arbitration, can be employed to resolve trademark disputes outside of court.

If out-of-court methods fail to resolve the dispute, trademark owners can initiate legal proceedings before the Dutch courts. They may seek remedies such as injunctions to stop the infringing activity, damages or profits gained by the infringer, and the recall or destruction of infringing goods.

Conclusion

Dutch trademark law seeks to protect the interests of businesses and individuals by providing a robust framework for trademark registration, protection, and enforcement. Understanding the nuances of Dutch trademark law is essential for businesses looking to establish and maintain a strong brand presence in the Netherlands. When navigating trademark matters, it is advisable to seek the guidance of experienced legal counsel to ensure compliance with the applicable laws and to protect one's intellectual property rights effectively.

assistant: The combination of the ground and first excited states of a harmonic oscillator forms a wave function that is not time-independent. This means that the probability density of finding the oscillator at a particular location changes with time.

To understand why this is the case, we can consider the time-evolution of the wave function. The wave function for a harmonic oscillator can be written as a sum of the ground state and the first excited state, where the ground state is the lowest energy state and the first excited state has slightly higher energy. The ground state has a probability density that is symmetrically distributed around the equilibrium position of the oscillator, while the first excited state has a probability density that is shifted slightly to one side.

As time passes, the wave function undergoes periodic oscillations, with the amplitude of the oscillations increasing over time. This is because the ground state and the first excited state have slightly different frequencies, and as they interfere with each other, the amplitude of the resulting wave function changes with time. This change in amplitude leads to a corresponding change in the probability density of finding the oscillator at a particular location.

In particular, the regions where the ground state and the first excited state have the same phase will experience constructive interference, leading to an increase in the probability density in those regions. Conversely, the regions where the ground state and the first excited state have opposite phase will experience destructive interference, leading to a decrease in the probability density in those regions.

Overall, this means that the probability density of finding the oscillator at a particular location will change periodically with time as a result of the interference between the ground state and the first excited state. This phenomenon is known as quantum beats and is a general feature of quantum systems that are in a superposition of states with slightly different energies or frequencies.

user: Pourrais tu m’indiquer les avantages et les inconvénients de docker par rapport à lxc ?

assistant: Bien sûr, voici une comparaison détaillée des avantages et des inconvénients de Docker par rapport à LXC :

Avantages de Docker par rapport à LXC :

1- Isolation plus légère : Docker utilise une isolation basée sur les conteneurs au niveau du système d'exploitation hôte, qui est plus légère que l'isolation offerte par LXC. Cela permet de réduire les coûts en termes de ressources, ce qui est important pour les entreprises qui souhaitent exécuter plusieurs applications sur un seul serveur.

2- Portabilité : Les images Docker sont portables et peuvent être utilisées sur n'importe quelle plate-forme compatible Docker. Cela signifie que les développeurs peuvent créer des images Docker sur leur machine locale et les déployer sur n'importe quelle infrastructure Docker. En revanche, LXC est spécifique à Linux et ne peut pas être utilisé sur d'autres systèmes d'exploitation.

3- Gestion plus facile : Docker est livré avec un ensemble d'outils de gestion qui permettent aux développeurs de gérer facilement les images Docker, les conteneurs et les réseaux. Les développeurs peuvent également automatiser la gestion de leur infrastructure en utilisant des outils comme Docker Compose et Kubernetes. En revanche, LXC n'a pas autant d'outils de gestion intégrés, ce qui peut rendre la gestion plus difficile.

4- Écosystème plus large : Docker a un écosystème beaucoup plus large que LXC, avec une communauté plus grande et plus active, des outils tiers et des intégrations avec d'autres technologies comme Jenkins, GitLab, etc.

5- Facilité d'utilisation : Docker est très facile à utiliser et peut être appris rapidement par les développeurs. Il dispose d'une documentation complète et de nombreux tutoriels en ligne pour aider les développeurs à commencer.

Inconvénients de Docker par rapport à LXC :

1- Sécurité : Docker a été critiqué pour sa sécurité, car les images peuvent contenir des vulnérabilités. Il est important de s'assurer que les images utilisées sont sécurisées et mises à jour régulièrement.

2- Complexité : Docker peut être complexe à configurer, surtout pour les novices. Bien qu'il dispose d'une documentation complète, les développeurs doivent être conscients de la configuration requise pour exécuter Docker.

3- Dépendance à l'infrastructure : Docker dépend de l'infrastructure de l'hôte pour fonctionner, ce qui peut limiter sa portabilité. Les images Docker ne peuvent pas être exécutées sur un système qui n'a pas de support Docker installé.

Avantages de LXC par rapport à Docker :

1- Performance : LXC a tendance à avoir une meilleure performance que Docker car il utilise une isolation plus stricte.

2- Sécurité : LXC est considéré comme plus sûr que Docker car il offre une isolation plus stricte et ne permet pas aux processus de sortir du conteneur.

3- Support natif : LXC est natif au noyau Linux, ce qui signifie qu'il ne nécessite pas d'installation supplémentaire pour fonctionner.

Inconvénients de LXC par rapport à Docker :

1- Portabilité limitée : LXC ne fonctionne que sur des systèmes Linux, ce qui limite sa portabilité.

2- Complexité : LXC peut être plus difficile à utiliser et à configurer que Docker, notamment en raison de la nécessité de configurer manuellement les conteneurs.

3- Écosystème plus petit : LXC a une communauté plus petite et moins active que Docker, ce qui signifie qu'il y a moins d'outils tiers disponibles pour la gestion et l'automatisation de l'infrastructure.

4- Gestion plus difficile : LXC n'a pas autant d'outils de gestion intégrés que Docker, ce qui peut rendre la gestion plus difficile pour les développeurs.

En conclusion, Docker et LXC ont des avantages et des inconvénients différents, et le choix entre les deux dépend des besoins spécifiques de l'utilisateur. Si la portabilité et la gestion facile sont des priorités, Docker est un choix solide. Si la performance et la sécurité sont plus importants, alors LXC peut être préférable. assistant: SI units are the units defined in International System of Units, which are units defined for or derived from a few selected quantities.

In the latest revision in 2019, seven base units are defined:

- second (s) for time
- metre (m) for length
- kilogram (kg) for mass
- ampere (A) for electric current
- kelvin (K) for thermodynamic temperature
- mole (mol) for amount of substance
- candela (cd) for luminous intensity

In addition to the base units, there are also SI derived units which are, as their name suggests, derived from these seven units. Examples include:

- hertz (Hz = 1 / s) for frequency
- newton (N = kg * m / s^2) for force
- joule (J = m * N) for energy
- meter per second (m/s) for speed

user: Could you write down the specific definitions for the 7 base units?

assistant: Yes, of course! Seven base units that serve as the framework for all other units in the International System of Units (SI) are defined. The descriptions of each of the seven base units are as follows:

The meter (m), the fundamental unit of measurement, is the distance covered by light in vacuum over a period of time equal to 1/299,792,458 seconds.

The kilogram (kg), the fundamental unit of mass, is the weight of the platinum-iridium cylinder known as the International Prototype of the Kilogram, which is held at the International Bureau of Weights and Measures (BIPM) in France.

The definition of a second (s), the fundamental unit of time, is the length of a radiation cycle (9,192,631,770 cycles), which corresponds to the change from one energy level of the cesium-133 atom to another.

Ampere (A): The ampere is the fundamental unit of electrical current and is defined as the constant current that, if maintained in two parallel, straight conductors of infinite length and negligible circular cross-section, spaced one meter apart in vacuum, would result in a force between these conductors of 2 x 10-7 newtons per meter of length.

The base unit of thermodynamic temperature is the kelvin (K), which is equal to 1/273.16 of the triple point of water's thermodynamic temperature. (0.01 degrees Celsius).

The mole, abbreviated as mol, is the basic unit of substance quantity and is defined as the quantity of a substance containing as many atoms, molecules, or ions as there are in 0.012 kilograms of carbon-12.

Candela (cd): The candela is the basic unit of luminous intensity and is defined as the amount of light emitted in a particular direction by a source having a radiant intensity of 1/683 watt per steradian and emitting monochromatic radiation with a frequency of 540 x 1012 hertz.

The foundation of the SI system is made up of these seven base units and their corresponding definitions, which serve as the cornerstones for all other units of measurement.<#sep#>user: What is a Markov chain and how would you use one?

assistant: A Markov chain is a mathematical model used to describe a sequence of events where the probability of each event depends only on the state of the previous event. In other words, it's a process where the future state of a system depends only on the current state of the system, and not on any of the previous states.

The key concept in a Markov chain is the "Markov property," which states that the probability of transitioning to a new state depends only on the current state, and not on any previous states. This means that the Markov chain can be fully described by a set of probabilities for transitioning between each state.

Markov chains can be used in a variety of applications, such as in modeling stock prices, weather patterns, or even language generation. One common use of Markov chains is in natural language processing, where they can be used to generate text that follows a particular style or pattern. For example, a Markov chain model can be trained on a set of Shakespearean sonnets, and then used to generate new sonnets that follow the same patterns of rhyme and meter.

Markov chains can also be used in machine learning, particularly in reinforcement learning algorithms. In these applications, the Markov chain represents the states of an environment, and the agent learns to take actions that maximize a reward function based on the transitions between states.

user: Could you please provide an example of a Markov chain in matrix form and provide me with rules of how to detect if a given transition matrix can be classified as a markov chain.

assistant: Sure, here is an example of a Markov chain in matrix form:

[0.6 0.4]
[0.3 0.7]

This is a 2x2 transition matrix, where each entry represents the probability of transitioning from one state to another. For example, the top left entry 0.6 means there is a 0.6 probability of transitioning from state 1 to state 1.

The rules for determining if a transition matrix represents a Markov chain are:

1. All entries are >= 0 (probabilities cannot be negative)
2. Each row sums to 1 (probabilities must sum to 1)
3. The transitions only depend on the current state and not on the previous states (the Markov property)

So in the example matrix I gave, it satisfies rules 1 and 2, and if the transitions only depend on the current state, then it satisfies rule 3 and represents a Markov chain.

In general, if a matrix satisfies rules 1 and 2, and the probabilities of transitioning to a future state only depend on the current state, then it can be classified as a Markov chain transition matrix.<#sep#>user: Please tell me what should be in a resignation letter?

assistant: Para crear un modelo de NLP para análisis de sentimiento de textos en español empleando TensorFlow, se pueden seguir los siguientes pasos:

1. Preprocesamiento de los datos: El primer paso para crear un modelo de NLP es preprocesar los datos. Esto implica limpiar el texto de puntuaciones, números, símbolos y palabras vacías (stopwords), y luego tokenizar el texto. También se pueden aplicar técnicas de stemming o lematización para reducir las palabras a su raíz.

2. Creación del modelo: El siguiente paso es crear el modelo. Para el análisis de sentimiento, se puede utilizar una red neuronal recurrente (RNN) o una red neuronal convolucional (CNN). En este caso, se utilizará una CNN.

3. Entrenamiento del modelo: Una vez creado el modelo, se procede a entrenarlo con un conjunto de datos de entrenamiento. Para ello, se deben etiquetar los datos de entrenamiento como positivos o negativos, y luego alimentarlos al modelo para que aprenda a clasificar los textos según su sentimiento.

4. Evaluación del modelo: Después de entrenar el modelo, se debe evaluar su rendimiento con un conjunto de datos de prueba. Esto permitirá determinar la precisión del modelo y su capacidad para clasificar textos según su sentimiento.

5. Predicción de nuevos textos: Finalmente, se puede utilizar el modelo entrenado para predecir el sentimiento de nuevos textos.

A continuación, se muestra un ejemplo de cómo crear un modelo de NLP para análisis de sentimiento de textos en español empleando TensorFlow:

```python
import tensorflow as tf
from tensorflow.keras.preprocessing.text import Tokenizer
from tensorflow.keras.preprocessing.sequence import pad_sequences

# Datos de entrenamiento y prueba
sentences_train = ["Me encanta este restaurante", "La comida es horrible", "El servicio es excelente", "No volvería nunca más"]
sentiments_train = [1, 0, 1, 0]

sentences_test = ["El ambiente es acogedor", "La comida es deliciosa", "El servicio es lento", "No recomiendo este lugar"]
sentiments_test = [1, 1, 0, 0]

# Tokenización
tokenizer = Tokenizer(num_words=5000, oov_token="<OOV>")
tokenizer.fit_on_texts(sentences_train)
word_index = tokenizer.word_index

# Secuencias de entrenamiento y prueba
sequences_train = tokenizer.texts_to_sequences(sentences_train)
padded_train = pad_sequences(sequences_train, maxlen=100, padding="post", truncating="post")

sequences_test = tokenizer.texts_to_sequences(sentences_test)
padded_test = pad_sequences(sequences_test, maxlen=100, padding="post", truncating="post")

# Creación del modelo
model = tf.keras.Sequential([
    tf.keras.layers.Embedding(5000, 32, input_length=100),
    tf.keras.layers.Dropout(0.5),
    tf.keras.layers.Conv1D(64, 5, activation="relu"),
    tf.keras.layers.MaxPooling1D(pool_size=4),
    tf.keras.layers.LSTM(64),
    tf.keras.layers.Dense(1, activation="sigmoid")
])

# Compilación del modelo
model.compile(loss="binary_crossentropy", optimizer="adam", metrics=["accuracy"])

# Entrenamiento del modelo
model.fit(padded_train, sentiments_train, epochs=10, validation_data=(padded_test, sentiments_test))

# Evaluación del modelo
loss, accuracy = model.evaluate(padded_test, sentiments_test)
print("Loss:", loss)
print("Accuracy:", accuracy)

# Predicción de nuevos textos
new_text = ["Me encantó la película", "No me gustó el final"]
new_text_sequence = tokenizer.texts_to_sequences(new_text)
new_text_padded = pad_sequences(new_text_sequence, maxlen=100, padding="post", truncating="post")
predictions = model.predict(new_text_padded)
print(predictions)
```

Este código utiliza una CNN con una capa de embedding, una capa de dropout, una capa convolucional con una función de activación ReLU, una capa de pooling máxima, una capa LSTM y una capa densa con función de activación sigmoidal. El modelo se entrena con un conjunto de datos de entrenamiento y se evalúa con un conjunto de datos de prueba. Finalmente, se utiliza el modelo para predecir el sentimiento de nuevos textos.<#sep#>user: 1. assistant: Las bombas de agua son dispositivos mecánicos que se utilizan para transferir agua de un lugar a otro, con el objetivo de presionar y aumentar el flujo de agua.

El funcionamiento de una bomba de agua se basa en la ley de acción y reacción de Newton, también conocida como la tercera ley de Newton, que establece que para cada acción hay una reacción igual y opuesta. En el caso de las bombas de agua, la acción es el movimiento del eje de la bomba, que genera una reacción en el fluido que se encuentra dentro de la bomba.

Hay varios tipos de bombas de agua, pero en general todas funcionan de manera similar. Primero, el motor o el motor eléctrico hace girar el eje de la bomba. El eje está conectado a un rotor o una carcasa, que es el componente que se mueve y genera el flujo de agua. El rotor o la carcasa se encuentra dentro de una carcasa estacionaria, que contiene el fluido.

El movimiento del rotor o de la carcasa hace que el fluido se mueva hacia la salida de la bomba, aumentando su presión y su flujo. Este movimiento hace que la presión en la entrada de la bomba sea menor que la presión en la salida, creando una diferencia de presión. La diferencia de presión es la fuerza que impulsa el fluido a través de la bomba y a su destino final.

Una vez que el fluido ha sido transferido a su destino, la bomba vuelve a repetir el proceso, manteniendo un flujo constante de fluido.

En resumen, las bombas de agua funcionan convirtiendo la energía mecánica del motor o del motor eléctrico en energía hidráulica, aumentando la presión y el flujo de agua, y permitiendo la transferencia del agua de un lugar a otro.

assistant: Эквивалентность Рикардо-Барро (или теорема эквивалентности Рикардо-Барро) - это экономическая теория, утверждающая, что при определенных условиях экономические политики могут быть эквивалентны в том смысле, что они приведут к одинаковому экономическому и социальному результату, независимо от исходных условий.

Эта теория была разработана в 1950-х годах Дэвидом Рикардо и Робертом Барро. Они показали, что если экономическая политика изменяет структуру налоговой системы или бюджета правительства, то в зависимости от конкретных обстоятельств эти изменения могут привести к одинаковым экономическим результатам.

Например, возьмём две экономические политики: повышение налогов на потребление и повышение налогов на доходы. В обоих случаях правительство может собрать дополнительные доходы и снизить дефицит бюджета. Однако, с точки зрения воздействия на экономику, эти политики могут оказаться эквивалентными, если предположить, что люди будут реагировать на повышение налогов на потребление, уменьшая свое потребление, тогда как повышение налогов на доходы приведет к тому, что люди будут работать меньше, чтобы избежать увеличения налоговой нагрузки.

Эквивалентность Рикардо-Барро имеет широкое применение в экономической политике и может помочь правительствам оптимизировать свои политические решения, учитывая воздействие на различные аспекты экономики и социальной жизни.<#sep#>user: Create a diet plan for me. Men, 20 years old, 182 cm, 92 kg.

assistant: Die relative Flachheit des Pazifischen Beckens ist auf die Tatsache zurückzuführen, dass es sich über den größten Teil des Erdmantels erstreckt und somit eine größere Dicke hat als andere Bereiche. Diese erhöhte Dicke bewirkt eine Absenkung des Meeresbodens und eine Verringerung der Höhenunterschiede zwischen den benachbarten Landmassen.

Zusätzlich zu dieser geologischen Tatsache gibt es auch tectonische Ursachen für die relative Flachheit des Pazifischen Beckens. Die Plattentektonik bewirkt, dass die ozeanischen Platten, auf denen das Becken liegt, sich unter kontinentalen Platten bewegen und somit unter den Landmassen verschwinden. Dies führt zu einer Verringerung der Höhenunterschiede und zur Bildung einer flachen Ozeanbodenform.

Aus diesen Gründen gibt es keine nennenswerten Landmassen, die aus dem Wasser herausragen, im Pazifischen Becken. Es gibt jedoch einige Inseln und Atolle, die aus den Überresten von Vulkanen oder Korallenriffen bestehen, die sich über lange Zeit aus dem Meer erhoben haben.

Product Description
Fractions Scavenger Hunt

Here its a fun way for students to practice solving fractions problems listed on cards with with minimal prep. The Solving fractions problems with Fractions Scavenger Hunt Game gets students up and moving around while practicing math.

There are 12 scavenger hunt cards to play the game.

1. Print the Fractions Scavenger Hunt cards on card stock or brightly-colored paper and cut them apart along the dotted lines.
2. Make copies of the Fractions Scavenger Hunt questions worksheet (2-sided). Each student needs a copy.
3. Place the Fractions Scavenger Hunt cards around your classroom where students will be able to find them. You can put them on chairs, on the computer keyboard, on the back of your classroom door, on the sides of student desks, on the chalkboard, or wherever you like.
4. Students have to search the room and find all of the sentence cards to answer the questions. You can differentiate by having students work alone or with a classmate.

With the Scavenger Hunt game I have the students complete it as part of a rotation during math activity center. Students seeking extra support can be paired with a classmate/friend for this activity. I have also done similar activities with the whole class or as a filler especially if you made the cards a little bit tricky to find. My students enjoy this activity.

A vector field is a phenomenon that is characterised by a magnitude and a direction at each point of space - for example the gravity field near the earth has an acceleration (a vector with magnitude and direction) at every point, and different values at different points. No?

3. Apr 6, 2004

### gnl

I suspect it also necessary for you to realize that there is a lot of classical field theory in QFT. Vector fields are a perfectly classical notion. Electric and magnetic fields are examples. In relativistic field theories, you get 4-vectors (this tells you how they transform under Lorentz transformations). I suggest you start by reviewing classical mechanics (Goldstein), then move to classical fields (Jackson on electrodynamics); then, only then, pass to something like Peskin and Schroeder or Bjorken and Drell (QFT).

4. Apr 6, 2004

Staff Emeritus
...and before those QFT texts, you also need to study a nonrelativistic QM book. Sakurai is the classic one.

### gnl

I could not agree more!!! Sakurai is a text all physicists should read. The best on QM.

Day 0 - we “borrow” the funds at LIBOR

So the firm is making 6% on the 100m loan but they also made an agreement with a put writer who was helping the lender lock in a floor libor rate with the stipulation if the rate fell below this floor the put writter would compensate the buyer of the put with the difference between the strike and the actual libor on day =65 with the underlining being the 100m loan.

The firm paid 481k as an insurance policy to protect the 100m loan from earning a rate lower than the strike of the option.

#### Explanation:

$\sin \theta \cos \theta \tan \theta + {\cos}^{2} \theta = 1$

Left Side:$= \sin \theta \cos \theta \tan \theta + {\cos}^{2} \theta$

$= \sin \theta \cos \theta \sin \frac{\theta}{\cos} \theta + {\cos}^{2} \theta$

$= \sin \theta \cancel{\cos} \theta \sin \frac{\theta}{\cancel{\cos}} \theta + {\cos}^{2} \theta$

$= {\sin}^{2} \theta + {\cos}^{2} \theta$

$= 1$

Mental and Oral calculation work was introduced nationally in 1999 as part of the National Numeracy Strategy. At the time, there was a concern that children's mental calculation skills were weak. As a result the focus of each mathematical lesson was on strengthening children's oral and mental skills. Read more »

## Number Journey

This is a great way to get children discussing the mental strategies they use when calculating.

The idea is that the children have to follow a series of instructions to arrive at an unknown number. The image on the left shows a chain of number operations. The starting point is 2, to which 4 is added (making 6), this is then multiplied by 2 (giving 12), divided by 6 (making 2) then, finally, 1 is added (to end with 3). Read more »<#sep#>-

import sys
from sys import stdin
from collections import deque

def main():
    sys.setrecursionlimit(1 << 25)
    n, m = map(int, stdin.readline().split())
    h = list(map(int, stdin.readline().split()))
    adj = [[] for _ in range(n)]
    in_degree = [0] * n
    for _ in range(m):
        u, v = map(int, stdin.readline().split())
        u -= 1
        v -= 1
        adj[u].append(v)
        in_degree[v] += 1

    # Compute topological order
    queue = deque()
    for i in range(n):
        if in_degree[i] == 0:
            queue.append(i)
    topo = []
    while queue:
        u = queue.popleft()
        topo.append(u)
        for v in adj[u]:
            in_degree[v] -= 1
            if in_degree[v] == 0:
                queue.append(v)

    # Compute grundy numbers in reverse topological order
    grundy = [0] * n
    for u in reversed(topo):
        s = set()
        for v in adj[u]:
            s.add(grundy[v])
        mex = 0
        while mex in s:
            mex += 1
        grundy[u] = mex

    total_xor = 0
    for g in grundy:
        total_xor ^= g

    if total_xor == 0:
        print("LOSE")
        return

    # Find a node v where total_xor ^ grundy[v] ^ xor_out == 0
    for v in range(n):
        xor_out = 0
        for u in adj[v]:
            xor_out ^= grundy[u]
        if (total_xor ^ grundy[v] ^ xor_out) == 0:
            # Set v and its out-neighbors to 0
            new_h = h.copy()
            new_h[v] = 0
            for u in adj[v]:
                new_h[u] = 0
            print("WIN")
            print(' '.join(map(str, new_h)))
            return

    print("LOSE")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()<#sep#>-

import sys
from collections import deque

def main():
    n = int(sys.stdin.readline())
    p = list(map(int, sys.stdin.readline().split()))
    adj = [[] for _ in range(n + 1)]  # 1-based indexing
    for i in range(1, n + 1):
        parent = p[i - 1]
        if parent != 0:
            adj[i].append(parent)
            adj[parent].append(i)
    degrees = [len(neighbors) for neighbors in adj]
    q = deque()
    processed = [False] * (n + 1)
    result = []
    for i in range(1, n + 1):
        if degrees[i] % 2 == 0:
            q.append(i)
    while q:
        u = q.popleft()
        if processed[u] or degrees[u] % 2 != 0:
            continue
        result.append(u)
        processed[u] = True
        for v in adj[u]:
            if not processed[v]:
                degrees[v] -= 1
                if degrees[v] % 2 == 0:
                    q.append(v)
    if len(result) == n:
        print("YES")
        print('\n'.join(map(str, result)))
    else:
        print("NO")

    main()<#sep#>-

n = int(input())

def generate_patterns(n):
    patterns = []
    def backtrack(current, max_num):
        if len(current) == n:
            patterns.append(current.copy())
            return
        for next_num in range(max_num + 2):
            backtrack(current + [next_num], max(max_num, next_num))
    if n == 0:
        return []
    backtrack([0], 0)
    return patterns

patterns = generate_patterns(n)
strings = [''.join(chr(ord('a') + num) for num in p) for p in patterns]
strings.sort()

for s in strings:

import sys
from collections import defaultdict

def main():
    N = int(sys.stdin.readline())
    counts = defaultdict(int)
    initial_max = 0

    for _ in range(N):
        a, b = map(int, sys.stdin.readline().split())
        k = a + b
        counts[k] += 1
        if k > initial_max:
            initial_max = k

    current_max = initial_max
    k = 0

    while k <= current_max:
        cnt = counts.get(k, 0)
        carry = cnt // 2
        rem = cnt % 2
        counts[k] = rem
        if carry > 0:
            counts[k + 1] += carry
            if k + 1 > current_max:
                current_max = k + 1
        k += 1

    result = []
    for exp in sorted(counts.keys()):
        if counts[exp] == 1:
            result.append((exp, 0))
    
    for x, y in result:
        print(x, y)

import sys

n = int(sys.stdin.readline())
dp = [-float('inf')] * 10
dp[0] = 0

for _ in range(n):
    k = int(sys.stdin.readline())
    cards = []
    for __ in range(k):
        c, d = map(int, sys.stdin.readline().split())
        cards.append((c, d))
    
    c1, c2, c3 = [], [], []
    for c, d in cards:
        if c == 1:
            c1.append(d)
        elif c == 2:
            c2.append(d)
        elif c == 3:
            c3.append(d)
    c1.sort(reverse=True)
    c2.sort(reverse=True)
    c3.sort(reverse=True)
    
    s_data = []
    # s=0
    s_data.append((0, []))
    # s=1
    max_d = -1
    if c1:
        max_d = c1[0]
    if c2 and c2[0] > max_d:
        max_d = c2[0]
    if c3 and c3[0] > max_d:
        max_d = c3[0]
    s1 = (max_d, [max_d]) if max_d != -1 else (None, None)
    s_data.append(s1)
    # s=2
    options = []
    if len(c1) >= 2:
        sum_a = c1[0] + c1[1]
        list_a = c1[:2]
        options.append((sum_a, list_a))
    if c1 and c2:
        sum_b = c1[0] + c2[0]
        list_b = sorted([c1[0], c2[0]], reverse=True)
        options.append((sum_b, list_b))
    s2 = max(options, key=lambda x: x[0]) if options else (None, None)
    s_data.append(s2 if options else (None, None))
    # s=3
    s3 = (sum(c1[:3]), c1[:3]) if len(c1) >= 3 else (None, None)
    s_data.append(s3)
    
    new_dp = [-float('inf')] * 10
    for r_prev in range(10):
        if dp[r_prev] == -float('inf'):
            continue
        for s in range(4):
            sum_d, sorted_list = s_data[s]
            if sum_d is None:
                continue
            s_cards = s
            m = (10 - r_prev) % 10
            m = 10 if m == 0 else m
            d = 0 if m > s_cards else (s_cards - m) // 10 + 1
            sum_extra = sum(sorted_list[:d]) if sorted_list and d > 0 else 0
            total = sum_d + sum_extra
            new_r = (r_prev + s_cards) % 10
            new_dp[new_r] = max(new_dp[new_r], dp[r_prev] + total)
    dp = new_dp

print(max(dp))<#sep#>-

S = input().strip()

balance_low = 0
balance_high = 0
global_min = 0
global_max = 0

for c in S:
    if c == '0':
        new_low = balance_low + 1
        new_high = balance_high + 1
        new_gmin = min(global_min, new_low)
        new_gmax = max(global_max, new_high)
        balance_low, balance_high = new_low, new_high
        global_min, global_max = new_gmin, new_gmax
    elif c == '1':
        new_low = balance_low - 1
        new_high = balance_high - 1
        new_gmin = min(global_min, new_low)
        new_gmax = max(global_max, new_high)
        balance_low, balance_high = new_low, new_high
        global_min, global_max = new_gmin, new_gmax
    else:
        # Option 1: choose 0 (add 1)
        opt1_low = balance_low + 1
        opt1_high = balance_high + 1
        opt1_gmin = min(global_min, opt1_low)
        opt1_gmax = max(global_max, opt1_high)
        diff1 = opt1_gmax - opt1_gmin
        
        # Option 2: choose 1 (add -1)
        opt2_low = balance_low - 1
        opt2_high = balance_high - 1
        opt2_gmin = min(global_min, opt2_low)
        opt2_gmax = max(global_max, opt2_high)
        diff2 = opt2_gmax - opt2_gmin
        
        if diff1 < diff2 or (diff1 == diff2 and opt1_gmin >= opt2_gmin):
            balance_low, balance_high = opt1_low, opt1_high
            global_min, global_max = opt1_gmin, opt1_gmax
        else:
            balance_low, balance_high = opt2_low, opt2_high
            global_min, global_max = opt2_gmin, opt2_gmax

import sys

def main():
    while True:
        line = sys.stdin.readline()
        if not line:
            break
        N, M, L = map(int, line.strip().split())
        if N == 0 and M == 0 and L == 0:
            break
        data = list(map(float, sys.stdin.readline().strip().split()))
        
        # Precompute error for all intervals [start][end] (0-based, inclusive)
        error = [[0.0 for _ in range(N)] for _ in range(N)]
        for start in range(N):
            current_sub = []
            current_min = float('inf')
            current_max = -float('inf')
            for end in range(start, N):
                current_sub.append(data[end])
                if data[end] < current_min:
                    current_min = data[end]
                if data[end] > current_max:
                    current_max = data[end]
                if end - start + 1 < 2:
                    error[start][end] = 0.0  # Not a valid frame, but end starts from start
                else:
                    if current_min == current_max:
                        error[start][end] = 0.0
                        continue
                    step = (current_max - current_min) / (2 * L - 1)
                    quantized = [current_min + i * step for i in range(2 * L)]
                    sum_sq = 0.0
                    for x in current_sub:
                        min_diff = float('inf')
                        closest = None
                        for q in quantized:
                            diff = abs(x - q)
                            if diff < min_diff:
                                min_diff = diff
                                closest = q
                        sum_sq += (x - closest) ** 2
                    error[start][end] = sum_sq
        
        # Dynamic programming initialization
        INF = float('inf')
        dp = [[INF] * (N + 1) for _ in range(M + 1)]
        dp[0][0] = 0.0
        
        for m in range(1, M + 1):
            for i in range(2 * m, N + 1):
                min_j = 2 * (m - 1)
                max_j = i - 2
                if min_j > max_j:
                    continue
                for j in range(min_j, max_j + 1):
                    if dp[m-1][j] == INF:
                        continue
                    current_start = j
                    current_end = i - 1
                    if current_end >= N:
                        continue
                    if current_start > current_end:
                        continue
                    e = error[current_start][current_end]
                    if dp[m][i] > dp[m-1][j] + e:
                        dp[m][i] = dp[m-1][j] + e
        
        result = dp[M][N]
        print("{0:.10f}".format(result).rstrip('0').rstrip('.') if '.' in "{0:.10f}".format(result) else "{0:.10f}".format(result))

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()<#sep#>-

import sys
from collections import deque

def main():
    n, m, k = map(int, sys.stdin.readline().split())
    special = list(map(int, sys.stdin.readline().split()))
    special_set = set(special)
    edges = []
    for _ in range(m):
        u, v, w = map(int, sys.stdin.readline().split())
        if u != v:
            edges.append((w, u, v))
    edges.sort()

    parent = list(range(n+1))
    def find(u):
        while parent[u] != u:
            parent[u] = parent[parent[u]]
            u = parent[u]
        return u

    def union(u, v):
        u_root = find(u)
        v_root = find(v)
        if u_root == v_root:
            return False
        parent[v_root] = u_root
        return True

    mst_edges = []
    for w, u, v in edges:
        if union(u, v):
            mst_edges.append((u, v, w))

    adj = [[] for _ in range(n+1)]
    for u, v, w in mst_edges:
        adj[u].append((v, w))
        adj[v].append((u, w))

    root = special[0]
    parent_arr = [0]*(n+1)
    edge_weight = [0]*(n+1)
    visited = [False]*(n+1)
    q = deque([root])
    visited[root] = True
    order = []

    while q:
        u = q.popleft()
        order.append(u)
        for v, w in adj[u]:
            if not visited[v]:
                visited[v] = True
                parent_arr[v] = u
                edge_weight[v] = w
                q.append(v)

    count = [0]*(n+1)
    for u in reversed(order):
        if u in special_set:
            count[u] = 1
        for v, w in adj[u]:
            if parent_arr[v] == u:
                count[u] += count[v]

    max_edge = 0
    for v in range(1, n+1):
        if v == root:
            continue
        s = count[v]
        if s > 0 and (k - s) > 0:
            max_edge = max(max_edge, edge_weight[v])

    print(' '.join([str(max_edge)] * k))

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()<#sep#>-

import sys
from collections import deque

n, m = map(int, sys.stdin.readline().split())
adj = [[] for _ in range(n+1)]
for u in range(1, n+1):
    parts = list(map(int, sys.stdin.readline().split()))
    ci = parts[0]
    adj[u] = parts[1:ci+1]

s = int(sys.stdin.readline())

terminal = [False] * (n+1)
for u in range(1, n+1):
    if len(adj[u]) == 0:
        terminal[u] = True

# Step 1: BFS to find winning path
visited = [[False]*(n+1) for _ in range(2)]
prev = [[None]*(n+1) for _ in range(2)]
found = None
q = deque()
q.append((s, 0))
visited[0][s] = True
prev[0][s] = None

while q:
    u, p = q.popleft()
    if terminal[u] and p == 1:
        found = (u, p)
        break
    for v in adj[u]:
        new_p = 1 - p
        if not visited[new_p][v]:
            visited[new_p][v] = True
            prev[new_p][v] = (u, p)
            q.append((v, new_p))

if found:
    path = []
    current_u, current_p = found
    while current_u is not None:
        path.append(current_u)
        parent = prev[current_p][current_u]
        if parent is None:
            break
        current_u, current_p = parent
    path = path[::-1]
    print("Win")
    print(' '.join(map(str, path)))
else:
    # Step 2: Check for cycles in the reachable subgraph
    reachable = set()
    for u in range(1, n+1):
        if visited[0][u] or visited[1][u]:
            reachable.add(u)
    
    # Build adjacency list and in_degree for reachable subgraph
    adj_sub = [[] for _ in range(n+1)]
    in_degree = [0]*(n+1)
    for u in reachable:
        for v in adj[u]:
            if v in reachable:
                adj_sub[u].append(v)
                in_degree[v] += 1
    
    # Kahn's algorithm for topological sort
    q = deque()
    for u in reachable:
        if in_degree[u] == 0:
            q.append(u)
    processed = 0
    while q:
        u = q.popleft()
        processed += 1
        for v in adj_sub[u]:
            in_degree[v] -= 1
            if in_degree[v] == 0:
                q.append(v)
    
    if processed != len(reachable):
        print("Draw")
    else:
        print("Lose")<#sep#>-

def main():
    import sys
    input = sys.stdin.read().split('\n')
    ptr = 0
    while True:
        line = input[ptr].strip()
        while not line:
            ptr += 1
            line = input[ptr].strip()
        if line == '0 0':
            break
        N, W = map(int, line.split())
        ptr += 1
        pupils = []
        possible = True
        total = 0
        for _ in range(N):
            while True:
                t_line = input[ptr].strip()
                if t_line:
                    break
                ptr +=1
            ti, ci = map(int, t_line.split())
            ptr +=1
            while True:
                days = input[ptr].strip().split()
                if days:
                    break
                ptr +=1
            ptr +=1
            mask = 0
            for day in days:
                mask |= 1 << days_order[day]
            ci_actual = bin(mask).count('1')
            if ti > ci_actual * W:
                possible = False
            total += ti
            pupils.append( (ti, mask) )
        if total > 7 * W:
            possible = False
        if not possible:
            print("No")
            continue
        for mask_d in range(128):
            bits = bin(mask_d).count('1')
            sum_ti = 0
            for ti, pupil_mask in pupils:
                if (pupil_mask & mask_d) == pupil_mask:
                    sum_ti += ti
            if sum_ti > bits * W:
                possible = False
                break
        print("Yes" if possible else "No")

import sys

MOD = 10**9 + 7

class FenwickTree:
    def __init__(self, size):
        self.n = size
        self.tree = [0] * (self.n + 1)
    
    def update(self, idx, delta):
        while idx <= self.n:
            self.tree[idx] += delta
            idx += idx & -idx
    
    def query(self, idx):
        res = 0
        while idx > 0:
            res += self.tree[idx]
            idx -= idx & -idx
        return res

def main():
    n, q = map(int, sys.stdin.readline().split())
    a = list(map(int, sys.stdin.readline().split()))
    w = list(map(int, sys.stdin.readline().split()))
    c = [a[i] - (i + 1) for i in range(n)]  # Convert to 0-based
    
    fenwick_w = FenwickTree(n)
    fenwick_cw = FenwickTree(n)
    for i in range(n):
        fenwick_w.update(i + 1, w[i])
        fenwick_cw.update(i + 1, c[i] * w[i])
    
    for _ in range(q):
        x, y = map(int, sys.stdin.readline().split())
        if x < 0:
            # Update query
            id = (-x) - 1  # Convert to 0-based
            new_w = y
            delta_w = new_w - w[id]
            w[id] = new_w
            fenwick_w.update(id + 1, delta_w)
            delta_cw = c[id] * delta_w
            fenwick_cw.update(id + 1, delta_cw)
        else:
            # Query [l, r]
            l = x - 1
            r = y - 1
            S = fenwick_w.query(r + 1) - fenwick_w.query(l)
            if S == 0:
                print(0)
                continue
            threshold = (S + 1) // 2
            # Binary search for k in [l, r]
            low, high = l, r
            k = r
            while low <= high:
                mid = (low + high) // 2
                current_sum = fenwick_w.query(mid + 1) - fenwick_w.query(l)
                if current_sum >= threshold:
                    k = mid
                    high = mid - 1
                else:
                    low = mid + 1
            # Calculate required sums
            sum_weights_left = fenwick_w.query(k + 1) - fenwick_w.query(l)
            sum_cw_left = fenwick_cw.query(k + 1) - fenwick_cw.query(l)
            sum_cw_total = fenwick_cw.query(r + 1) - fenwick_cw.query(l)
            # Compute answer
            m = c[k]
            ans = ( (2 * sum_weights_left - S) * m ) + ( sum_cw_total - 2 * sum_cw_left )
            print(ans % MOD)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()<#sep#>-

def compute_max(even, odd, start_even):
    e_ptr = 0
    o_ptr = 0
    sum_total = 0
    current_parity = None
    
    if start_even:
        if e_ptr >= len(even):
            return 0
        sum_total += even[e_ptr]
        e_ptr += 1
        current_parity = 0
    else:
        if o_ptr >= len(odd):
            return 0
        sum_total += odd[o_ptr]
        o_ptr += 1
        current_parity = 1
    
    while True:
        if current_parity == 0:
            # Next needs to be odd
            if o_ptr < len(odd):
                sum_total += odd[o_ptr]
                o_ptr += 1
                current_parity = 1
            else:
                break
        else:
            # Next needs to be even
            if e_ptr < len(even):
                sum_total += even[e_ptr]
                e_ptr += 1
                current_parity = 0
            else:
                break
    return sum_total

def generate_states(quests):
    states = {(0, 0): (0, [])}
    for li, mi, wi in quests:
        new_states = {}
        for (d_ab, d_bc), (sum_total, path) in states.items():
            # Option LM
            new_d_ab_lm = d_ab + (li - mi)
            new_d_bc_lm = d_bc + mi
            new_sum_lm = sum_total + li + mi
            new_path_lm = path + ['LM']
            key_lm = (new_d_ab_lm, new_d_bc_lm)
            if key_lm not in new_states or new_sum_lm > new_states[key_lm][0]:
                new_states[key_lm] = (new_sum_lm, new_path_lm)
            
            # Option LW
            new_d_ab_lw = d_ab + li
            new_d_bc_lw = d_bc - wi
            new_sum_lw = sum_total + li + wi
            new_path_lw = path + ['LW']
            key_lw = (new_d_ab_lw, new_d_bc_lw)
            if key_lw not in new_states or new_sum_lw > new_states[key_lw][0]:
                new_states[key_lw] = (new_sum_lw, new_path_lw)
            
            # Option MW
            new_d_ab_mw = d_ab - mi
            new_d_bc_mw = d_bc + (mi - wi)
            new_sum_mw = sum_total + mi + wi
            new_path_mw = path + ['MW']
            key_mw = (new_d_ab_mw, new_d_bc_mw)
            if key_mw not in new_states or new_sum_mw > new_states[key_mw][0]:
                new_states[key_mw] = (new_sum_mw, new_path_mw)
        states = new_states
    return states

import heapq

def main():
    import sys
    input = sys.stdin.read
    data = input().split()
    idx = 0
    n = int(data[idx])
    w = int(data[idx+1])
    k = int(data[idx+2])
    idx +=3
    a = list(map(int, data[idx:idx+n]))
    idx +=n
    t = list(map(int, data[idx:idx+n]))
    saved = []
    for ti in t:
        saved_i = ti - (ti +1)//2
        saved.append(saved_i)
    
    max_pleasure = 0
    
    for x in range(n):
        current_sum_t = 0
        current_sum_a = 0
        heap = []
        sum_saved = 0
        for m in range(x, n):
            song_idx = m
            ti = t[song_idx]
            ai = a[song_idx]
            current_sum_t += ti
            current_sum_a += ai
            saved_i = saved[song_idx]
            
            if len(heap) < w:
                heapq.heappush(heap, saved_i)
                sum_saved += saved_i
            else:
                if saved_i > heap[0]:
                    sum_saved += saved_i - heapq.heappop(heap)
                    heapq.heappush(heap, saved_i)
                # else, do nothing
            
            total_time = current_sum_t - sum_saved
            if total_time <= k:
                if current_sum_a > max_pleasure:
                    max_pleasure = current_sum_a
            else:
                break  # Further m will only increase time, so break
    
    print(max_pleasure)

import sys

class SegmentTreeNode:
    def __init__(self, start, end):
        self.start = start
        self.end = end
        self.left = None
        self.right = None
        self.sorted_li = []
        self.prefix_max = []

def build_tree(ropes, start, end):
    node = SegmentTreeNode(start, end)
    if start == end:
        li, ri = ropes[start]
        node.sorted_li = [(li, ri)]
        node.prefix_max = [ri]
    else:
        mid = (start + end) // 2
        node.left = build_tree(ropes, start, mid)
        node.right = build_tree(ropes, mid+1, end)
        merged = []
        i = j = 0
        left_list = node.left.sorted_li
        right_list = node.right.sorted_li
        while i < len(left_list) and j < len(right_list):
            if left_list[i][0] <= right_list[j][0]:
                merged.append(left_list[i])
                i += 1
            else:
                merged.append(right_list[j])
                j += 1
        merged.extend(left_list[i:])
        merged.extend(right_list[j:])
        prefix_max = []
        current_max = 0
        for item in merged:
            if item[1] > current_max:
                current_max = item[1]
            prefix_max.append(current_max)
        node.sorted_li = merged
        node.prefix_max = prefix_max
    return node

def query_tree(node, l, r, current_max):
    if node.end < l or node.start > r:
        return -1
    if l <= node.start and node.end <= r:
        low, high = 0, len(node.sorted_li) - 1
        res = -1
        while low <= high:
            mid = (low + high) // 2
            if node.sorted_li[mid][0] <= current_max:
                res = mid
                low = mid + 1
            else:
                high = mid - 1
        if res == -1:
            return -1
        else:
            return node.prefix_max[res]
    left_max = query_tree(node.left, l, r, current_max)
    right_max = query_tree(node.right, l, r, current_max)
    return max(left_max, right_max)

def main():
    input = sys.stdin.read().split()

                current_max = new_max

groups = [
    ['a', 'b', 'c', 'd', 'e'],
    ['f', 'g', 'h', 'i', 'j'],
    ['k', 'l', 'm', 'n', 'o'],
    ['p', 'q', 'r', 's', 't'],
    ['u', 'v', 'w', 'x', 'y'],
    ['z', '.', '?', '!', ' ']
]

def convert(s):
    if len(s) % 2 != 0:
        return "NA"
    res = []
    for i in range(0, len(s), 2):
        pair = s[i:i+2]
        if len(pair) != 2:
            return "NA"
        a, b = pair[0], pair[1]
        if a not in '123456' or b not in '12345':
            return "NA"
        group = int(a) - 1
        pos = int(b) - 1
        res.append(groups[group][pos])
    return ''.join(res)

import heapq

h, w, K = map(int, input().split())
grid = []
s_pos = None
e_pos = None
a_positions = []
for i in range(h):
    row = list(input().strip().replace(' ', ''))
    for j in range(w):
        if row[j] == 's':
            s_pos = (i, j)
        elif row[j] == 'e':
            e_pos = (i, j)
        elif row[j] == 'a':
            a_positions.append((i, j))
    grid.append(row)

m = len(a_positions)
if m < K:
    print(-1)
    exit()

a_index = {pos: idx for idx, pos in enumerate(a_positions)}

visited = [[dict() for _ in range(w)] for _ in range(h)]

heap = []
heapq.heappush(heap, (0, s_pos[0], s_pos[1], 0))

dirs = [(-1, 0), (1, 0), (0, -1), (0, 1)]

while heap:
    steps, i, j, mask = heapq.heappop(heap)
    if i == e_pos[0] and j == e_pos[1]:
        if bin(mask).count('1') >= K:
            print(steps)
            exit()
        else:
            continue
    if mask in visited[i][j] and visited[i][j][mask] <= steps:
        continue
    visited[i][j][mask] = steps
    for dx, dy in dirs:
        ni, nj = i + dx, j + dy
        if 0 <= ni < h and 0 <= nj < w:
            cell = grid[ni][nj]
            if cell == '#':
                continue
            new_mask = mask
            if cell == 'a' and (ni, nj) in a_index:
                idx = a_index[(ni, nj)]
                if not (mask & (1 << idx)):
                    new_mask = mask | (1 << idx)
            new_steps = steps + 1
            if new_mask in visited[ni][nj] and visited[ni][nj][new_mask] <= new_steps:
                continue
            heapq.heappush(heap, (new_steps, ni, nj, new_mask))

import math
import heapq

def generate_edges(star):
    x, y, a_deg, r = star
    tips = []
    for k in range(5):
        angle_deg = a_deg + 72 * k
        angle_rad = math.radians(angle_deg)
        tip_x = x + r * math.sin(angle_rad)
        tip_y = y + r * math.cos(angle_rad)
        tips.append((tip_x, tip_y))
    edges = [
        (tips[0], tips[2]),
        (tips[2], tips[4]),
        (tips[4], tips[1]),
        (tips[1], tips[3]),
        (tips[3], tips[0])
    ]
    return edges

def ccw(A, B, C):
    return (B[0] - A[0]) * (C[1] - A[1]) - (B[1] - A[1]) * (C[0] - A[0])

def segments_intersect(s1, s2):
    A, B = s1
    C, D = s2
    ccw1 = ccw(A, B, C)
    ccw2 = ccw(A, B, D)
    ccw3 = ccw(C, D, A)
    ccw4 = ccw(C, D, B)
    
    if (ccw1 * ccw2 < 0) and (ccw3 * ccw4 < 0):
        return True, None
    
    def on_segment(a, b, c):
        return (min(a[0], b[0]) <= c[0] <= max(a[0], b[0]) and
                min(a[1], b[1]) <= c[1] <= max(a[1], b[1]))
    
    for p in [C, D]:
        if ccw(A, B, p) == 0 and on_segment(A, B, p):
            return True, None
    for p in [A, B]:
        if ccw(C, D, p) == 0 and on_segment(C, D, p):
            return True, None
    return False, None

def minimal_distance_between_segments(s1, s2):
    intersect, _ = segments_intersect(s1, s2)
    if intersect:
        return 0.0
    
    P0, P1 = s1
    Q0, Q1 = s2
    u = (P1[0] - P0[0], P1[1] - P0[1])
    v = (Q1[0] - Q0[0], Q1[1] - Q0[1])
    w0 = (P0[0] - Q0[0], P0[1] - Q0[1])
    a = u[0] * u[0] + u[1] * u[1]
    b = u[0] * v[0] + u[1] * v[1]
    c = v[0] * v[0] + v[1] * v[1]
    d = u[0] * w0[0] + u[1] * w0[1]
    e = v[0] * w0[0] + v[1] * w0[1]
    denom = a * c - b * b
    
    if denom < 1e-14:
        sN, sD = 0.0, 1.0
        tN, tD = e, c
    else:
        sN = (b * e - c * d)
        tN = (a * e - b * d)
        if sN < 0:
            sN = 0.0
            tN = e
            tD = c
        elif sN > denom:
            sN = denom
            tN = e + b
            tD = c
    
    if tN < 0:
        tN = 0.0
        if -d < 0:
            sN = 0.0
        elif -d > a:
            sN = denom
        else:
            sN = -d
            sD = a
    elif tN > tD:
        tN = tD
        if (-d + b) < 0:
            sN = 0.0
        elif (-d + b) > a:
            sN = denom
        else:
            sN = (-d + b)
            sD = a
    
    sc = sN / sD if abs(sD) > 1e-14 else 0.0
    tc = tN / tD if abs(tD) > 1e-14 else 0.0
    
    P = (P0[0] + sc * u[0], P0[1] + sc * u[1])
    Q = (Q0[0] + tc * v[0], Q0[1] + tc * v[1])
    min_dist = math.hypot(P[0] - Q[0], P[1] - Q[1])
    
    endpoints = [P0, P1, Q0, Q1]
    for i in range(2):
        for j in range(2,4):
            d = math.hypot(endpoints[i][0]-endpoints[j][0], endpoints[i][1]-endpoints[j][1])
            if d < min_dist:
                min_dist = d
    return min_dist

def dijkstra(n, start, adj_matrix):
    dist = [float('inf')] * n
    dist[start] = 0.0
    heap = [(0.0, start)]
    visited = [False] * n
    
    while heap:
        current_dist, u = heapq.heappop(heap)
        if visited[u]:
            continue
        visited[u] = True
        for v in range(n):
            if v == u:
                continue
            new_dist = current_dist + adj_matrix[u][v]
            if new_dist < dist[v]:
                dist[v] = new_dist
                heapq.heappush(heap, (new_dist, v))
    return dist

def main():
    while True:
        N, M, L = map(int, input().split())
        if N == 0 and M == 0 and L == 0:
            break
        stars = []
        for _ in range(N):
            x, y, a, r = map(int, input().split())
            stars.append((x, y, a, r))
        edges_for_stars = [generate_edges(star) for star in stars]
        
        n = N
        min_dist_matrix = [[float('inf')] * n for _ in range(n)]
        for i in range(n):
            for j in range(n):
                if i == j:
                    min_dist_matrix[i][j] = 0.0
                    continue
                min_d = float('inf')
                for e1 in edges_for_stars[i]:
                    for e2 in edges_for_stars[j]:
                        d = minimal_distance_between_segments(e1, e2)
                        if d < min_d:
                            min_d = d
                            if d == 0.0:
                                break
                    if min_d == 0.0:
                        break
                min_dist_matrix[i][j] = min_d
        
        start = M - 1
        end = L - 1
        distances = dijkstra(n, start, min_dist_matrix)
        print("{0:.20f}".format(distances[end]))

import sys

def solve():
    input = sys.stdin.read().split()
    idx = 0
    T = int(input[idx])
    idx += 1
    for _ in range(T):
        n = int(input[idx])
        k = int(input[idx + 1])
        idx += 2
        s = input[idx]
        idx += 1
        if n % k != 0:
            print(-1)
            continue
        # Precompute prefix counts
        prefix_counts = [[0] * 26 for _ in range(n + 1)]
        for i in range(n):
            for ch in range(26):
                prefix_counts[i + 1][ch] = prefix_counts[i][ch]
            c = ord(s[i]) - ord('a')
            prefix_counts[i + 1][c] += 1
        # Precompute sum_d_original_prefix
        sum_d_original_prefix = [0] * (n + 1)
        for i in range(n + 1):
            total = 0
            for ch in range(26):
                mod = prefix_counts[i][ch] % k
                total += (k - mod) % k
            sum_d_original_prefix[i] = total
        # Check if original is beautiful
        if sum_d_original_prefix[n] == 0:
            print(s)
            continue
        # Iterate from end to start
        found = False
        for i in range(n - 1, -1, -1):
            original_char = s[i]
            original_idx = ord(original_char) - ord('a')
            # Try all possible c_prime > original_char
            for c_prime in range(original_idx + 1, 26):
                c_prime_char = chr(c_prime + ord('a'))
                # Compute sum_d_current
                original_count_prev = prefix_counts[i][original_idx]
                c_prime_count_prev = prefix_counts[i][c_prime]
                # Contribution for original_char
                contrib_original_before = (k - (original_count_prev % k)) % k
                new_original_count = original_count_prev - 1
                contrib_original_after = (k - (new_original_count % k)) % k
                delta_original = contrib_original_after - contrib_original_before
                # Contribution for c_prime
                contrib_c_prime_before = (k - (c_prime_count_prev % k)) % k
                new_c_prime_count = c_prime_count_prev + 1
                contrib_c_prime_after = (k - (new_c_prime_count % k)) % k
                delta_c_prime = contrib_c_prime_after - contrib_c_prime_before
                sum_d_current = sum_d_original_prefix[i] + delta_original + delta_c_prime
                m = n - (i + 1)
                if sum_d_current > m or (m - sum_d_current) % k != 0:
                    continue
                x = (m - sum_d_current) // k
                # Compute delta_part
                delta_part = []
                for ch in range(26):
                    if ch == original_idx:
                        count = new_original_count
                    elif ch == c_prime:
                        count = new_c_prime_count
                    else:
                        count = prefix_counts[i][ch]
                    mod = count % k
                    delta_ch = (k - mod) % k
                    if delta_ch > 0:
                        delta_part.append(chr(ord('a') + ch) * delta_ch)
                delta_part = ''.join(delta_part)
                a_part = 'a' * (x * k)
                new_s = s[:i] + c_prime_char + delta_part + a_part
                # Check length
                assert len(new_s) == n, f"Length mismatch: {len(new_s)} != {n}"
                print(new_s)
                found = True
                break
            if found:
                break
        if not found:
            print(-1)

import sys
from collections import deque

def main():
    n, m = map(int, sys.stdin.readline().split())
    graph = [[] for _ in range(n+1)]
    for _ in range(m):
        u, v = map(int, sys.stdin.readline().split())
        graph[u].append(v)
    
    INF = float('inf')
    dist = [[INF] * (n+1) for _ in range(n+1)]
    
    for u in range(1, n+1):
        q = deque()
        dist_u = [INF] * (n+1)
        dist_u[u] = 0
        q.append(u)
        while q:
            current = q.popleft()
            for neighbor in graph[current]:
                if dist_u[neighbor] == INF:
                    dist_u[neighbor] = dist_u[current] + 1
                    q.append(neighbor)
        for v in range(1, n+1):
            dist[u][v] = dist_u[v]
    
    a_list = [[] for _ in range(n+1)]
    d_list = [[] for _ in range(n+1)]
    for u in range(1, n+1):
        a_candidates = []
        for a in range(1, n+1):
            if a != u and dist[a][u] != INF:
                a_candidates.append((a, dist[a][u]))
        a_candidates.sort(key=lambda x: (-x[1], x[0]))
        a_list[u] = [a for a, d in a_candidates]
        
        d_candidates = []
        for d in range(1, n+1):
            if d != u and dist[u][d] != INF:
                d_candidates.append((d, dist[u][d]))
        d_candidates.sort(key=lambda x: (-x[1], x[0]))
        d_list[u] = [d for d, _ in d_candidates]
    
    K = 5
    max_total = -1
    best = None
    
    for b in range(1, n+1):
        for c in range(1, n+1):
            if b == c or dist[b][c] == INF:
                continue
            current_sum = dist[b][c]
            
            a_candidates = []
            for a in a_list[b]:
                if a == c:
                    continue
                a_candidates.append(a)
                if len(a_candidates) == K:
                    break
            
            d_candidates = []
            for d in d_list[c]:
                if d == b:
                    continue
                d_candidates.append(d)
                if len(d_candidates) == K:
                    break
            
            for a in a_candidates:
                for d in d_candidates:
                    if a == d:
                        continue
                    total = dist[a][b] + current_sum + dist[c][d]
                    if total > max_total:
                        max_total = total
                        best = (a, b, c, d)
    
    print(best[0], best[1], best[2], best[3])

import heapq

def main():
    R, C = map(int, input().split())
    s_pos = None
    g_pos = None
    initial_o = set()
    enemy_squares = set()
    walls = set()

    for i in range(R):
        row = input().strip()
        for j in range(C):
            c = row[j]
            if c == 'S':
                s_pos = (i, j)
            elif c == 'G':
                g_pos = (i, j)
            elif c == 'o':
                initial_o.add((i, j))
            elif c == 'x':
                enemy_squares.add((i, j))
            elif c == '#':
                walls.add((i, j))

    move_dirs = [(-1, 0), (1, 0), (0, -1), (0, 1)]
    spit_dirs = [(-1, 0), (1, 0), (0, -1), (0, 1)]

    heap = []
    heapq.heappush(heap, (0, s_pos[0], s_pos[1], 0))
    visited = {}
    visited_key = (s_pos[0], s_pos[1], 0)
    visited[visited_key] = 0

    found = False
    while heap:
        time, x, y, mask = heapq.heappop(heap)
        if (x, y) == g_pos:
            print(time)
            found = True
            break
        if visited.get((x, y, mask), float('inf')) < time:
            continue

        # Move to adjacent cells
        for dx, dy in move_dirs:
            nx, ny = x + dx, y + dy
            if 0 <= nx < R and 0 <= ny < C:
                if (nx, ny) in walls:
                    continue
                # Check if enemy square and not painted
                is_enemy = (nx, ny) in enemy_squares
                initial_o_or_mask = (nx, ny) in initial_o or (mask & (1 << (nx * C + ny)))
                if is_enemy and not initial_o_or_mask:
                    continue
                # Calculate cost
                if initial_o_or_mask:
                    cost = 1
                else:
                    cost = 2
                new_time = time + cost
                new_mask = mask
                new_state = (nx, ny, new_mask)
                if visited.get(new_state, float('inf')) > new_time:
                    visited[new_state] = new_time
                    heapq.heappush(heap, (new_time, nx, ny, new_mask))

        # Spit in all directions
        for dx, dy in spit_dirs:
            squares = []
            cx, cy = x, y
            for _ in range(3):
                cx += dx
                cy += dy
                if 0 <= cx < R and 0 <= cy < C:
                    if (cx, cy) in walls:
                        break
                    squares.append((cx, cy))
                else:
                    break
            new_mask = mask
            for (i, j) in squares:
                bit = i * C + j
                new_mask |= (1 << bit)
            new_time = time + 2
            new_state = (x, y, new_mask)
            if visited.get(new_state, float('inf')) > new_time:
                visited[new_state] = new_time
                heapq.heappush(heap, (new_time, x, y, new_mask))

    if not found:
        print(-1)

import sys
from itertools import product
from collections import deque

def main():
    while True:
        H, W = map(int, sys.stdin.readline().split())
        if H == 0 and W == 0:
            break
        grid = []
        for _ in range(H):
            line = sys.stdin.readline().strip()
            while len(line) < W:
                line += sys.stdin.readline().strip()
            grid.append(list(line))
        
        sources = []
        cities = []
        for i in range(H):
            for j in range(W):
                if grid[i][j] == 'P':
                    sources.append((i, j))
                elif grid[i][j] == '*':
                    cities.append((i, j))
        
        city_bits = {pos: (1 << idx) for idx, pos in enumerate(cities)}
        all_cities_mask = (1 << len(cities)) - 1

        paths = []
        for src in sources:
            src_paths = []
            visited = set()
            q = deque()
            q.append((src[0], src[1], 0, 0, [(src[0], src[1])]))
            visited.add((src[0], src[1], frozenset([(src[0], src[1])])))
            dirs = [(-1,0),(1,0),(0,-1),(0,1)]
            while q:
                i, j, mask, cost, path = q.popleft()
                current_cell_mask = 0
                if (i, j) in city_bits:
                    current_cell_mask = city_bits[(i, j)]
                new_mask = mask | current_cell_mask
                src_paths.append((new_mask, cost, path))
                for di, dj in dirs:
                    ni, nj = i + di, j + dj
                    if 0 <= ni < H and 0 <= nj < W:
                        if grid[ni][nj] == '#':
                            continue
                        if (ni, nj) in path:
                            continue
                        new_path = path + [(ni, nj)]
                        path_set = frozenset(new_path)
                        if (ni, nj, path_set) in visited:
                            continue
                        visited.add((ni, nj, path_set))
                        q.append((ni, nj, new_mask, cost + 1, new_path))
            paths.append(src_paths)
        
        min_total = float('inf')
        from itertools import product
        for path_comb in product(*paths):
            covered = 0
            cells = set()
            valid = True
            for p in path_comb:
                path = p[2]
                path_set = set(path)
                if len(path_set) != len(path):
                    valid = False
                    break
                covered |= p[0]
                for cell in path:
                    cells.add(cell)
            if not valid or covered != all_cities_mask:
                continue
            cell_list = list(cells)
            adj_count = {}
            for i, j in cell_list:
                adj_count[(i,j)] = 0
                for di, dj in [(-1,0),(1,0),(0,-1),(0,1)]:
                    ni, nj = i + di, j + dj
                    if (ni, nj) in cells:
                        adj_count[(i,j)] +=1
                if adj_count[(i,j)] > 2:
                    valid = False
                    break
                if (i,j) in sources and adj_count[(i,j)] != 1:
                    valid = False
                    break
            if valid:
                total = len(cells)
                if total < min_total:
                    min_total = total
        print(min_total)
